tagline: The old mail road past salt ponds and stone walls.
intro: Route 1 follows the old Post Road about twelve miles across South Kingstown, from the open land, farms, marinas and woods south of the Wakefield cutoff to the houses and shops of the northern stretch. Half a mile in the middle belongs to Narragansett and is left out of the count.

It began as a web of Indian trails used for centuries, and in colonial days it carried the mail and the newspapers. About four miles of stone walls run beside it, and on clear days Aquidneck Island and Newport show across Narragansett Bay.

moments.title: Willow Dell
moments.text: Just west of Matunuck Beach Road a stone marker on the south side of the highway shows the Wager Weeden Memorial Fountain, at a farm the Weeden family has held since 1826.

moments.title: Point Judith Pond
moments.text: From the road the view takes in Point Judith Pond, a shallow salt pond four miles long lying behind the barrier beaches.

moments.title: Hannah Robinson Tower
moments.text: The CCC's 40-foot wooden tower marks McSparran Hill, where Hannah Robinson, carried home failing in 1773 after eloping against her father's wishes, asked to stop and look over her homeland.
